title: Create LTS release notes generator (slower-change format) from PR labels + curated summaries
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
We need an LTS-specific release notes generator that produces enterprise-friendly, “slower-change” notes for each LTS patch (e.g., 1.18.1-lts) with: categorized changes, perf notes, upgrade notes, known issues/workarounds, and compatibility matrix. Output should be suitable for publishing in docs + linking from Console/Helm annotations.

Context
- LTS patches are intentionally small, high-scrutiny backports. Customers expect highly structured notes and explicit risk/compatibility guidance.
- We already generate mainline changelogs, but LTS needs different taxonomy and stricter metadata.

Primary inputs
1) GitHub PR labels and PR body fields
- Labels (proposed; implemented in ENG-4823):
  - lts/backport (required for inclusion)
  - lts/security (CVE or security advisory)
  - lts/sev1, lts/sev2 (incident severity driving inclusion)
  - release-notes:perf, release-notes:stability, release-notes:packaging, release-notes:docs
  - component:kernel, component:scheduler, component:kv-cache, component:packaging, component:ci
2) Curated summaries
- For each included PR, Release Manager can optionally supply a short, customer-readable summary (1–3 sentences) and “why it matters” line.
- If not provided, generator uses PR title + sanitized PR description (strip internal links and Slack references).
3) Known issues block
- Pull from the living known issues doc (short-term: checked-in markdown snippet referenced by path; long-term: Confluence sync).
- Known issues MUST include affected versions, symptom, mitigation/workaround, and fix plan (backport vs doc-only).

Output format (markdown) must follow Confluence taxonomy:
- sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/runtime-lts-release-notes-format-and-taxonomy.json
Required sections
- Header: version, release date, commit/tag, support window link, artifact verification pointers
- Summary: 3–6 bullet highlights (customer-readable)
- Changes by category (only backported items)
  - Security
  - Stability/Correctness
  - Performance (must include perf gate summary + caveats)
  - Packaging/Deploy (Private installer/Helm)
  - Observability/Operations
  - Documentation
- Compatibility matrix (minimum): runtime patch ↔ supported CUDA/toolchain baseline, GPU SKUs validated, minimum Redwood Private installer/Helm chart versions (if applicable)
- Upgrade notes
  - Breaking/behavioral changes (should be rare; must call out explicitly)
  - Recommended rollout procedure (Hosted/Dedicated/Private differences)
  - Rollback notes (what is safe to roll back, what isn’t)
- Known issues & workarounds (from known issues source; filter to versions <= current)
- Checksums/provenance pointers
  - Link to artifact checksums/provenance file and verification instructions

Non-goals
- Replacing mainline release notes tooling.
- Automatically deciding what should be included in an LTS patch (that’s the release manager’s job); generator compiles from labels + explicit include list.

Implementation notes
- Add “LTS mode” to existing release notes generator CLI.
- Generator should accept:
  - --channel=lts
  - --release-tag=runtime-1.18.1-lts (or equivalent)
  - --base-tag=runtime-1.18.0-lts
  - --include-prs=<comma-separated PR numbers> (optional override)
  - --known-issues-file=<path>
  - --compat-matrix-file=<path>
  - --output=<path>
- Deterministic output ordering (by category, then PR number) so notes are reviewable in PR.
- Produce a machine-readable companion artifact (flat JSON or CSV) for Console linking (short-term: embed in markdown frontmatter; long-term: publish alongside docs build).

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Can generate release notes for a patch tag using only repo + GitHub API
- [x] Categories and required headers match LTS taxonomy
- [x] Includes perf gate summary section (even if “No material change; within thresholds”), with link placeholder to perf-canary artifact
- [x] Known issues section is included and filtered appropriately
- [x] Supports manual curated summaries without editing generated output directly (i.e., edit a small config file committed with release PR)
- [x] Deterministic output (stable sorting)
- [x] Reviewed by Docs owner (Elliot) + Product (Marissa) for customer readability

References
- Epic: ENG-4821 Runtime LTS initiative
- Backport labels: ENG-4823
- Release branch CI: ENG-4824
- Release PR (first patch): sources/github/redwood/pr-23510-runtime-lts-1-18-1-release-notes-and-tags.json
- Generator implementation PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-23277-release-notes-generator-lts-mode.json
implementation_plan:
1) Extend generator CLI with --channel=lts and an LTS template renderer.
2) Add label-to-category mapping table (configurable).
3) Add support for curated summaries via a checked-in YAML/CSV (release manager owns updates).
4) Add known issues ingestion from a repo path (initially manual copy from Confluence doc).
5) Add compatibility matrix ingestion from repo path (maintained by Quentin).
6) Output markdown to release/ notes directory and (optionally) a small metadata file for Console/Helm.
7) Wire generator into release branch workflow (ENG-4824) so notes are generated in the release PR and reviewed like code.
testing_notes:
Unit tests
- label mapping → correct category buckets
- deterministic ordering (golden file snapshots)
- sanitization removes internal-only links (Slack, Linear, internal Confluence IDs when not public)

Integration tests
- run against a known tag pair and fixture PR data
- ensure empty categories render as omitted (except required sections)

Manual validation
- run generator for the first LTS patch candidate and compare with human-written draft; iterate until readability is acceptable for enterprise customers.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: PR labels aren’t consistently applied → missing items.
Mitigation: generator supports explicit include list; release manager checklist requires label review.

Risk: known issues source drifts / stale.
Mitigation: treat known issues as an explicit input file referenced in release PR; release manager must update before tagging.

Risk: perf gate link/data not available at note-generation time.
Mitigation: allow placeholder link; release PR must update with perf-canary artifact URL before publish.
ship_checklist:
Release manager steps (when cutting patch)
- Ensure all backported PRs have lts/backport label + correct release-notes category labels
- Update curated summaries file for any PR titles that aren’t customer-ready
- Update known issues file (add new items discovered in pilot; remove fixed items)
- Update compatibility matrix file if validation coverage changed
- Run generator and commit output as part of release PR
- Get signoff from Runtime + SRE + Docs on generated notes
comments: 2025-01-23 (Connor O'Brien): Assigning to Devon. We need this before the first LTS patch so the release PR is mostly mechanical. Please coordinate with Elliot for language/tone and with Marissa for required metadata that Console will link to.
2025-01-28 (Devon Price): Drafted label→category mapping; waiting on final label set from ENG-4823. In the meantime, I’ll build the template renderer and keep mapping configurable via a file.

2025-02-03 (Elliot Price): Please make sure the generator supports “curated summaries” because PR titles like “refactor scheduler gate” aren’t customer-facing. Also: add explicit ‘Upgrade notes’ even when empty; enterprise reviewers look for the section every time.

2025-02-06 (Marissa Cole): Console will likely show a ‘Release notes’ link next to LTS version pinning. We need stable URLs and a short summary block at the top that’s readable without scrolling. Also, call out any throughput tradeoff explicitly (even if expected).

2025-02-10 (Devon Price): Implemented LTS mode in generator; added frontmatter with version/date/tag fields and a top summary bullets section. Known issues are loaded from a provided file path so release PR can pin the exact content used at publish time.

2025-02-12 (Allison Grant): For perf notes: include p50/p95 latency and throughput deltas vs previous LTS patch and list the benchmark suite name + GPU SKUs covered. Even if within threshold, state ‘within ±X% gate’. Link to perf-canary artifact.

2025-02-14 (Connor O'Brien): Merged PR-23277. Marking ticket done. Follow-up: we should add a lint check in release PR template that fails if ‘Known issues’ is missing or points to a non-existent file.

2025-02-21 (Devon Price): Closed out. Generator is now used in the first LTS patch release PR; output is deterministic and supports curated summaries + known issues injection. Any additional Console metadata output can be a follow-up ticket if Product wants JSON instead of frontmatter.
